Patient walked in frustrated after a surgeon visit. His MRI showed bursitis and shoulder inflammation, and the response was: this is what happens when you get older, accept it.

His sister, older than him and pain-free, sat right there. Doctor doubled down anyway.

I hear this too often, and I’m going to be direct about it: aging doesn’t come with mandatory pain or limitation. Almost always there’s something to work with, whether that’s restoring movement, reducing pain, or helping someone move better than they have in years.

Getting older means something completely different when you’ve got the right support and the right approach. It means performing at your best at any age. Not settling.

If a doctor’s told you “this is just how it’s going to be,” that’s a signal to learn something different about what’s actually possible.

DM me. Let’s find out.
